dossier.public_summary: The dip changes essentially to zero or null depths in different sectors and even between individual predicted transits, with deep odd/even differences. This instability and spot-like 12947 ppm variability in sector 72 favour scattered bad/spot-contaminated events over a true planet, so the 13-day signal is best explained as noise/variability rather than a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 203.4% between sectors (chi2 56.55 dof 2) with sector 46 at -757 +-1755 ppm vs sector 72 at 17568 +-1708 ppm.
same TESS-SPOC product shows instability: verified with tool call returning verdict changes_within_a_source and p_constant_all 5.188424309425396e-13.

Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent (chi2 97.5130819 dof 5); outliers at 19750 ppm, -3121 ppm, -685 ppm, 19593 ppm at epoch -2, 0, -1, 55, with share_of_top_3 0.999 indicating a few events drive the signal.
Odd depths 6333 ppm vs even 12250 ppm differ at 3.007 sigma with depth_ratio 1.9 and sector_oe_max_sigma 6.219, favouring EB at twice the period.
Corroborates non-planet nature; low rank with no on_target centroid (verdict inconclusive, no sector with a clear difference image) and plausible neighbours at 37 arcsec, etc., but 0 within 1px.
